title: Brass Orchestral Repertoire
description: Intensive exploration of staple brass orchestra repertoire, emphasizing the works of important 19th and 20th century composers. Classes include rehearsal sessions, guided listening and analysis, mock auditions, resume and taped audition preparation.

title: Violin Ensemble

title: Viola Choir
description: The Viola Choir studies literature written or arranged for viola ensemble, perfecting elements of technique, intonation and interpretation. Works prepared by the Viola Choir will be performed in public and in studio recitals.

title: Cello Choir
description: The cello choir studies cello literature in depth, including duos, trios, quartets and larger cello ensemble works. Cellists work together on blend of sound, perfecting technique and intonation, as well as balance.The choir prepares works for public performances.

description: The ensemble will study a variety of Brazilian musical forms sharing a strong African influence with complex layers of interlocking syncopation, melodies emerging from the alternation of various drums, and a distinctively heavy swing.

title: Group Studies
description: Student-directed discussion and study in a variety of subjects within Music Composition.

title: Music Colloquium
description: Students receiving credit will present talks in their fiel on material arranged in consultation with the instructor. Credit assigned by the instructor will reflect the extent and quality of participation.

title: Individual Instruction in Composition
description: Individual instruction in composition, usually for one hour per week.

title: Analysis: Materials
description: Small group instruction in theoretical subjects (harmony, composition, orchestration, etc.).

title: Analysis: Forms
description: Small group instruction in musical forms and their development.

title: Special Topics in Music Composition
description: Individual or small group instruction in selected subjects related to the study of Music Composition, including but not limited to individual composers and their works, special compositional techniques, performance projects, and topics in technological applications to music.

title: Algorithmic Composition with Max/MSP
description: A formalized journey into the basics of algorithmic composition, using Max/MSP as a tool to aid the artist and engineer alike. We explore how simple algorithmic models can provide intriguing sonic results across all genres. These methods are not only useful for schematic problem solving but can also be good for expanding musical and creative thinking.

title: Art Song
description: Explorations of text setting, repertory, effective accompaniments. Content will vary by instructor.

title: The Classical Guitar in Contemporary Composition
description: A survey of modern classical guitar repertoire, considering the very nature of the genre and its relationship to popular music, the classical tradition, and contemporary composition at large. Classes consist of active listening, discussion, and score-study. The culmination is a short, original classical guitar composition. A background in music helpful, but no specific experience is required.

title: The Electric Guitar in Contemporary Composition
description: A survey of modern electric guitar repertoire, considering the very nature of the genre and its relationship to rock, classical, and contemporary composition at large. Classes consist of active listening, discussion, and score-study. The culmination is a short, original electric guitar composition. A background in music helpful, but no specific experience is required.

title: Favorite Things
description: Students will analyze and present their favorite works, whether acoustic or electronic; tonal or atonal or serial; chamber or orchestral or vocal. Subsequently, students will write music of their own, based on a single, well-defined element from the works they admire.

title: Language Lost: Music Creation and the Destruction of Meaning
description: How can composers maintain expressiveness in vocal music when specific meanings are elusive? We will focus on the manipulation of sound/speech qualities such as pitch, rhythm, phrasing, timbre, and tempo. Our multidisciplinary approach aims to both create and deconstruct language, exploring new technologies to enhance individual expression and innovate in musical communication.

title: Landscape Music
description: A study of music written in response to the natural and the built landscape(s) around us.

title: 1960S MUSICAL REVOLUTIONARIES: MILES DAVIS, JIMI HENDRIX, YOKO ONO, AND KARLHEINZ STOCKHAUSEN
description: Delves into the iconic 1960s, exploring the revolutionary impact of major figures Miles Davis, Jimi Hendrix, Yoko Ono, and Karlheinz Stockausen in their particular and overlapping domains. It offers a mix of music history and performative collaboration, welcoming students from all disciplines, regardless of their musical background.

title: CCS Musical
description: Collaborative class for the creation of new musical theater works. Content will vary by instructor.
